newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy supreme court to decide venue in Nazi case.
newsitem.headline: Italy supreme court to decide venue in Nazi case.

text.p: Italy's highest court convened on Monday to decide whether a civilian or a military court should hear the war crimes re-trial of former Nazi SS captain Erich Priebke.
Both forms of court have said they do not have jurisdiction and the case has been without a forum since the verdict reached at Priebke's first trial was thrown out on appeal last October.
Priebke, 83, is accused of complicity in multiple murder for his role in the SS massacre of 335 men and boys at the Ardeatine Caves near Rome on March 24, 1944. Seventy-five of the victims were Jews.
The Court of Cassation, Italy's supreme court, met at a closed hearing and has five days to rule on jurisdiction.
Civil plaintiffs, representing family members of victims, want Priebke tried in civilian court because they feel it would give a more stringent reading of the case than military court.
The defence has said it will seek another military trial, arguing that the Nazi SS was the military police force.
Priebke admits shooting two victims and crossing names off a list but said he had to follow orders or be killed himself.
He also says the massacre was a legitimate wartime reprisal for a partisans' bomb attack in Rome the previous day which killed 33 soldiers loyal to Nazi occupying forces.
At his first trial which ended on August 1, a military court found Priebke guilty but ordered him freed, citing extenuating circumstances which triggered an expired statute of limitations.
He was rearrested that night after relatives of the massacre's victims laid seige to the courthouse and is still being held in a military prison.
The Court of Cassation will also decide jurisdiction for Priebke's co-defendant, former SS major Karl Hass.

Hass had been an unwilling prosecution witness at Priebke's first trial. He tried to avoid testifying by leaving Rome the day before he was to appear, but fell from the balcony of his hotel and broke his pelvis. He later testified from hospital.
Hass, 84, who is under house arrest at a private clinic near Rome where he has been recovering, was charged along with Priebke because he too admitted a role in the massacre.
Priebke has been jailed in Rome since November 1995 when he was extradited to Italy from Argentina, where he had lived openly since 1948.
